title: HiTOP Factorization Hierarchy
description: Versioned hierarchy of core concepts, partial mappings, and local collections. Children encode factorization-specific hasTier edges; level is descriptive. See docs/factorizations.md.

hierarchy.description: Root node of the factorization tree. May be null only while meta.status is "draft" and the tree has not been populated yet.

factorization_id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier matching the factorizations/<factorization_id> directory name.

version.description: Version identifier matching the leading <version>_hierarchy.yaml filename segment and the v<N> directory, for example "V1052k" in v1/V1052k_hierarchy.yaml.

source.description: Origin of the factor structure, for example a source image or dataset path.

paper.description: Citation for the publication this factorization is derived from.

ontology_iri.description: IRI of the core ontology this factorization resolves codes against.

ontology_version.description: owl:versionInfo value of the ontology release the codes were resolved against.

commit.description: Optional git commit hash pinning the exact ontology state the codes were resolved against.

created_by.description: Identified creators. A legacy name string is accepted for compatibility.

created_at.description: Date this factorization version was created.

notes.description: Optional free-text provenance notes, for example differences from a previous version.

contributors.description: People contributing specifically to this factorization.

contributions.description: Persistent URI of the central contribution record.

level.description: Free-text hitop:hasLevel value naming the role this node plays in this factorization (for example Superspectrum, Spectrum, Subfactor, Component, or a factorization-specific refinement such as Sub-subfactor). Not restricted to a fixed vocabulary and not checked for depth consistency: real HiTOP branches legitimately skip levels (e.g. a Spectrum going straight to Component without an intervening Subfactor), so the same label can occur at different depths across a tree. Vertical ordering itself comes entirely from `children` nesting (hitop:hasTier), not from this value.

kind.description: concept (default): exact core concept with optional local wording; partial: local construct partially overlapping the core concept identified by code, without asserting equivalence or direction; collection: local grouping. Only collection codes are exempt from core lookup.

label.description: Factorization-local wording. For concept this asserts the same meaning as the core concept; for partial it names the overlapping local construct; for collection it names the grouping.

code.description: Existing core code for concept and partial; stable local identifier for collection.

bridge.description: Documentation-only cross-loading to exact, case-sensitive labels of other nodes in this same factorization, including partial and collection nodes. Targets must exist uniquely; self-references and duplicate targets are forbidden. No additional hasTier edges are generated. Reciprocal bridges and cycles are allowed.

provisional.description: Marks this node's placement as tentative, independent of the file-level meta.status.

children.description: Child nodes one level step below this node, per hitop:hasTier. For a collection node, its children are exactly the existing concepts being synthesized.

id.description: Required for partial only: stable local identity, unique also against collection codes. Independent of the referenced core code.

mapping_note.description: Optional explanation of the overlap and differences, allowed only for partial nodes.

orcid.description: ORCID URI; the runtime validator also checks its checksum.
